exact_items: Prompt_Pipeline.md should remain the owner of the effective-resolution field family and which requested/effective runtime identity fields exist and what they mean
storage-plan.md should remain the owner of persisted execution/runtime record families and where requested/effective identity is stored for attempts and current runtime projections

Executor_Protocol.md should own which execution-scoped context is required for scheduler/executor correctness: minimum execution-unit identity/runtime anchors needed for dispatch, retry, blocked handling, and receipts
orchestrator-subagent-integration.md should stop owning a canonical mixed runtime object; it should consume canonical execution/runtime context by reference
notes: The highest-risk duplication is requested/effective runtime identity being defined three times: prompt pipeline, storage, and tier context
This seam is now mostly an ownership cleanup, not a concept invention problem

exact_items: tier_runtime_record may survive, but only as a derived current-view/runtime-overlay projection, not as canonical source for execution identity, retry lineage, approval/recovery targeting, or usage truth
Recast tier_runtime_record as a current-view/runtime-overlay projection rather than the canonical execution owner
storage-plan.md still has both attempt_record and tier_runtime_record; tier_runtime_record should become clearly derived/view-oriented rather than the place where runtime identity hides
Run_Graph_View.md still repeatedly treats tier_id as the main per-node correlation key for output filtering, verification event filtering, usage links, copy/open actions, and event drill-in

Orchestrator_Page.md still describes the page as 'Progress / Tiers / Node Graph / Evidence / History / Ledger' and many data-source rows still bind live state to TierChanged, tier_id, tier-scoped evidence
The surface docs are behaving as if tier_runtime_record is canonical, even though attempt_record and blocked/runtime records hold canonical execution truth
stale_tokens: tier_id (as main per-node correlation key in Run_Graph_View)

exact_items: Introduce execution_unit_context as the canonical runtime-facing context object and make TierContext explicitly derived or compatibility-only

Canonical execution_unit_context minimum shape: project_id, run_id, thread_id?, feature_seam_id?, work_package_id?, node_id, attempt_id?, blocked_sequence?, replan_generation, execution_role, scheduler_lane, manual_priority?, safe_point_id?, remediation lineage refs, lane_id?, worktree_id?, workspace_ref, snapshot_ref?, requested/effective runtime identity, runtime state hooks
Refactor orchestrator-subagent-integration.md so selector and hook APIs consume: canonical execution-unit refs for truth and a smaller derived selection/decomposition object for heuristics
notes: Optional derived decomposition_context / selection_context can still carry: tier/view identity, heuristic inputs, parent-summary/dependency prompt conveniences
If TierContext survives at all, it should survive as a derived selection/view helper, not as the thing that owns canonical runtime identity

exact_items: persona_override_owner_id still allows tier_id-style ownership in shared runtime docs — likely needs a migration path toward run/node/attempt/subagent-owned scopes
Prompt_Pipeline.md still allows persona_override_owner_id scope values that include tier_id, which is increasingly a legacy ownership key for Orchestrator execution

human-in-the-loop.md is currently split across two models: older request state keyed by request_id, tier_id, tier_type; newer addenda acknowledging blocked_reason_code = waiting_approval and blocked_sequence
The important split is blocked-episode approval versus session-wide policy; the docs still do not formalize that boundary
pre-attempt blocked episodes must not invent an attempt_id; blocked_sequence is already the cleaner anchor

tier_runtime_record compatibility boundary: it should answer current visible progress state for tier-shaped UI grouping, latest active attempt or blocked episode pointer for this grouping, what progress tree / compact terminal / high-level tab badges should display
tier_runtime_record should NOT be treated as canonical source for execution identity, retry lineage, approval/recovery targeting, or usage truth
